techniques.evidence: crates/apps/connector-api-watch/tests/adoption.rs:77 The name and the doc comment claim the app's stamp is checked, but the assertions only check a struct the test built itself. scripts/docs/check-doc-sync.test.mjs:171 Uses the fixture that otherwise exits 2, so a status of 0 can only come from the stop_hook_active branch. The asserted value has one possible producer.

pairs.evidence: crates/core/src/governor.rs:383 The governor's parallelism claim (32 hosts did not serialize) is a wall-clock upper bound. That bound is what flips on a loaded machine, so the test is quarantined, and the fix (observe the sharded map's state instead) is still only an exit plan in the register.

techniques.evidence: crates/core/src/governor.rs:383 Overlap is proved with a stopwatch rather than an in-flight count or a barrier. This is the technique's measured failure, and it has landed in the flake register as the technique predicts.

crates/core/src/governor.rs:339 The .flake/register.json entry has an owner, entry date, expiry (2026-10-26), cause, evidence, exit plan and a written reason for skipped over muted. The test still runs nightly in long-lanes.

crates/core/tests/fetch_chokepoint.rs:231 The needle is a receiver-qualified field access, comment lines are dropped, wrapped chains are joined, and the inventory is checked both ways (line 283), which also makes an empty walk go red.
crates/core/tests/fetch_chokepoint.rs:153 The inventory explains a raw-engine row by the decision it keeps reachable: routing through ctx.fetch would assert the default arm.
crates/core/tests/host_memory_honesty.rs:28 A second host acts as a control, so a pass that wipes everything cannot satisfy the zombie-penalty test.

pairs.registryProposal: flake-lifecycle prefers muted over skipped, but libtest has no in-process muted form. This repo works around it by running the skipped set through a recorder on a nightly leg. The technique could name that as the accepted substitute for runners with no mute.
